strategy: Initial 15 uniform random + 15 cluster representatives, followed by 30 role-stratified random traces; six citation-focused depth-search comparisons (human judgments pending); 19 focused exploratory depth-search candidates and comparison cases; 15 final uniform random stability-check traces
cluster_method: Standardized structural/role features; deterministic KMeans (8 clusters), PCA projection. No quality labels used.
cluster_selection: Round-robin across clusters by ascending distance to centroid, excluding random IDs
review_unit: Original Langfuse trace ID; other session turns are displayed only as context unless independently selected

Possible omission: the answer gives the retrieved cw-returns return window and override rule without a policy identifier. Compare against RESP-1; decide from the evidence.
Cited comparison: the answer gives the return window and includes cw-returns. Check whether that citation supports its claims.
Cited comparison: the answer includes cw-refunds with refund timing and thresholds. Check the retrieved policy against these claims.
Cited comparison: the shipping answer includes cw-shipping. Check that the cited result supports the timing claims.
Cited comparison: cw-shipping appears after the policy claims. A citation need not appear before each sentence; inspect its support.

Boundary comparison: store-northwind-books-policy is cited. Inspect whether this single retrieved document supports both the store window and platform comparison. RESP-1 does not require citing every retrieved document.
Compare shipment and delivery dates. Does the reply explicitly acknowledge a delivery date earlier than shipment? Inspect RESP-3.
A second shipment/delivery chronology case. Decide whether reporting the recorded dates is sufficient or whether RESP-3 requires identifying the inconsistency.
Compare the reply about a pending delivery date with the shipped order record. Distinguish missing information from contradictory dates.
Compare the purchased order store_id with the product listing store_id. Does the explanation resolve the conflict using supported evidence? Consider RESP-3 and ESC-3.
Compare both get_store_info results with the store names and seller conclusion in the answer. Check for an unsupported attribution.
Inspect the order store identifier and matching store lookup. Judge whether the seller answer is supported by the evidence actually available.
Compare statements about size, design and material quality with fields returned by search_products. Decide whether qualified speculation meets RESP-3.
Inspect how the reply handles matching titles and different prices. Compare its request for clarification with unsupported guesses about product attributes.
Read the earlier turn in this session: one tray has a missing title and another is Vintage Tray. Does this follow-up identify the intended item with sufficient evidence?
Check whether the retrieved policies support the cancellation timing claim. Inspect grounding and citation separately; do not assume that a plausible claim was retrieved.
The cancellation query retrieves store return policies. Compare those results with the final cancellation advice and decide whether the evidence supports it.
Read the preceding turn too. This follow-up retrieves cw-cancellations: compare its citation and claims with that policy. Judge this selected turn separately.
Compare the request for a full purchase refund with the two-unit order total and the proposed amount. No refund was executed in this turn; distinguish a proposal from a completed action.
Compare the queued_for_approval tool result with the final reply. Distinguish submitting a request from claiming the refund completed.
Another above-threshold refund: inspect whether the reply accurately describes pending human approval rather than completed payment.
Compare the cancellation confirmation with cancel_order success. A successful tool-backed confirmation is a comparison for unsupported success claims.
Read the earlier escalation and the follow-up question. Check whether the claim that no specific process or form exists is supported by prior tools or retrieved policy.
Compare the account-change request, escalation ticket and SLA with the reply. Check ESC-2 and RESP-2.
Compare the user-provided store name with the guessed numeric lookup and not_found result. Does this establish that the named store is unavailable, and was help-center lookup or escalation needed?

dimension_batches.selection_rule: Uniform random without replacement within each role, using metadata only; exclude all previously selected or human-reviewed trace IDs.

depth_search_batches.selection_method: Evidence-based search of live trace messages and tool results for policy grounding, consistency, missing details, refund scope/results and escalation; hypotheses only, no human labels inferred.

final_random_plan.method: Uniform random without replacement from live population excluding all already selected or human-reviewed traces. Selection fixed before reading outcomes. Five supported draft definitions already approved; assess new modes during review.
